LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and Pattern Making, part of Creating and Executing in Grade 6 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why create rhythm in different beat patterns?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to /sing familiar songs and identify words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa,

2. tap/ clap/stamp and recite rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names,

3. relate the French rhythm names to the music note symbols for the crotchet, pair of quavers, minim, dotted minim, semibreve and their rests,

4. apply composition techniques to compose original rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names or note symbols, and their rests,

5. use digital resources to further their skills of creating rhythms,

6. listen to songs and identify songs in three -beat patterns,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to /sing familiar songs and identify words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa,
2. tap/ clap/stamp and recite rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names,
3. relate the French rhythm names to the music note symbols for the crotchet, pair of quavers, minim, dotted minim, semibreve and their rests,
4. apply composition techniques to compose original rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names or note symbols, and their rests,
5. use digital resources to further their skills of creating rhythms,
6. listen to songs and identify songs in three -beat patterns,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and Pattern Making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner combines various techniques to creatively come up with rhythmic patterns and

repeat patterns using block printing.

• Self-efficacy: The learner applies composition techniques to create and improvise original rhythmic patterns.
